ABSTRACT. The electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) is a promising approach for converting fossil fuel emissions into environmentally-sustainable chemicals and fuels. The ability to control the surface structure of CO2RR nanocatalysts provides an opportunity to tune product selectivity. Bimetallic gold-copper catalysts have been identified as emerging electrocatalyst candidates, but Cu incorporation typically lowers product selectivity compared with pure Au. Here we show sustained CO selectivity and activity up to 49% Cu content in small (<2nm), thiol-capped Au/Cu nanoparticles (NPs). Bimetallic NPs containing 49% Cu selectivity converted CO2 into CO with 100 ± 6% CO Faradaic efficiency and average mass activity of ~500 mA/mg during a 12-hour electrolysis experiment at -0.8V vs. RHE. Au/Cu NPs synthesized without thiol ligands selectively produced H2, whereas larger (>10 nm), thermally-dethiolated Au/Cu NPs produced a wider product distribution including H2, CO, and C2H4. Density functional theory (DFT) modelling of CO2RR and H2 evolution at realistic, thiol-capped Au/Cu NP structures indicated copper-thiol surface structures sustained CO selectivity by stabilizing key *CO intermediates while making *H binding less favorable. Calculations also predicted that removing a significant fraction of the thiol ligands would increase *CO binding strength such that desorption of CO product molecules could become the most thermodynamically challenging step. This result, coupled with increased *H stability on dethiolated nanocluster, points to decreased CO2RR selectivity for small, ligand-free catalysts, which is in line with experimental observations from out group and others. Our results demonstrate that thiol-ligand surface structures can sustain the CO selectivity of bimetallic Au/Cu NPs and reduce precious metal requirements for CO2RR.

sections.heading: INTRODUCTION
sections.text:
The electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) is an appealing strategy for addressing CO2 emissions because it can use excess renewable energy to produce carbon-neutral chemicals and fuels.1 The CO2RR has a rich structure-sensitivity, and recent efforts have focused on improving reaction rates and product selectivity by tuning the size, composition, crystallographic orientation, and active site density of nanostructured electrocatalysts.2-5 Gold can selectively convert CO2 into CO, 5,6 which is a versatile chemical building block that can be processed into a wide range of products, such as methanol, hydrocarbons, fuel additives, and plastics.6-8 Copper is another popular CO2RR catalyst because it is an earth abundant metal than can produce a variety of hydrocarbons and alcohols.9-11 However, Cu often demonstrates wide product distributions that will require additional chemical separation steps and reduce overall system efficiencies.
Bimetallic Au/Cu nanocatalysts have emerged as promising candidates for selective CO2 conversion with reduced precious metal content.12-19 Cu incorporation into Au can boost overall current density, but it can also decrease product selectivity. This presents practical challenges because costs associated with down-stream product separation may hinder large-scale deployment of CO2RR technologies. 20 From a fundamental perspective, the composition, surface structure, and specific arrangement of Au and Cu atoms have been predicted to impact electrochemical overpotentials, catalytic activity, and product selectivity.13,18,19 This presents opportunities for designing catalyst systems that maximize product selectivity and reduce precious metal requirements.
Organic capping ligands have been shown to stabilize specific surface structures that can influence CO2RR product distributions. 21-26 We used organo-thiol ligands to synthesize a series of monodisperse, sub-2nm Au/Cu NPs with unique copper-thiol surface moieties. Electron

In contrast to other reported Au/Cu catalysts,13-19 the thiol-capped Au/Cu NPs retained excellent CO selectivity and catalytic activity up to 49% Cu content.
Thiol-capped NPs containing 49% Cu demonstrated 94±5% CO Faradaic efficiency (FE) between -0.5V and -1.0V vs. RHE. A maximum CO mass activity ~1360 mA/mg and nearly quantitative CO FE (99.9%) was obtained at -1V vs. RHE. The 49% Cu NPs also showed sustained CO selectivity with 100 ± 6% CO FE at ~500 mA/mg during a 12-hour electrolysis experiment at -0.8V vs. RHE. Complementary DFT calculations with realistic, thiol-capped NP structures predicted Cu-thiol surface structures stabilized key CO2RR intermediates and reduced H2 evolution. In contrast, both experiment and theory indicate reduced CO2RR selectivity and increased H2 evolution at ligand-free NPs. Our combination of experiment and DFT modeling provides atomic-level structure-property relationships and demonstrates ligand-directed surface structuring as a design consideration for tuning the selectivity of CO2RR nanocatalysts.

Synthesis and Optical Spectroscopy. Au/Cu NPs were synthesized using a dendrimertemplate method developed by the Crooks group.27 Detailed synthetic procedures are presented in the Supporting Information. Briefly, aqueous Au3+ and Cu2+ ions were complexed inside G4PAMAM-OH dendrimers, reduced with NaBH4, and then extracted into toluene using 2- phenylethanethiol (PET) ligands. Deposition onto carbon black (CB). Thiol-capped NPs were dissolved in CH2Cl2 and sonicated with Vulcan XC-72R CB to achieve a final catalyst loading of 9 wt %. The PET ligands are not soluble in methanol, and NPs were precipitated onto the CB support by adding methanol. The resulting CB-supported NPs were then centrifuged, decanted, and re-sonicated in fresh methanol three times before drying under N2. CB-supported NP samples were used for TEM, X-ray spectroscopy, and electrochemical experiments. The CB provided a conductive support for electrochemical experiments, prevented charging during X-ray spectroscopy, and reduced particle coalescence during TEM imaging. Deposition onto the CB support did not change NP composition (Figure S1).
Transmission Electron Microscopy. High-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) imaging was conducted on a 200kV FEI Tecnai F20 TEM. sections.heading: CONCLUSIONS
sections.text:
We have studied the CO2RR and HER at thiol-capped Au/Cu NPs and observed selective CO2 conversion with reduced precious metal loadings. A combination of experimental work and computational modeling helped establish atomic-level structure-property relationships. For example, the presence of Cu atoms in the ligand-shell increased CO2RR Eonset due to less favorable *COOH formation at Cu-S ligand units. However, satisfactory stabilization of bound *CO intermediates coupled with unfavorable *H formation sustained CO2RR selectivity at reduced precious metal content. Experimental data showed somewhat reduced CO2RR selectivity and mass activity for Au/Cu NPs with high Cu content, and H2 evolution may become more significant as the precious metal content decreases towards zero. Finally, both experiment and theory indicate the absence of surface thiol units will increase H2 evolution due unfavorable desorption of strongly bound *CO intermediates and more favorable *H formation.
